Form One.main: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
Form One.competence: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
Form One.activity: (a) Describe the modern concept of atomic structure (Dalton’ s atomic structure and sub-atomic particles)

Form Two.competence: (b) Describe the concept of electronic arrangements
(c) Use the concept of atomic structure to determine the atomic and mass numbers of an element
(d) Explain the concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature (valence, oxidation state, radicals and naming of binary inorganic compounds using the IUP AC system)
(e) Determine empirical and molecular formulae of common compounds
(f) Describe the concept of chemical bonding (covalent and electrovalent bonding)
(g) Describe the concept of chemical reactions (chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, and types of chemical reactions)
(h) Relate the types of chemical reactions with common processes in daily life such as burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
(i) Describe acids, bases and salts (reactions of acids and bases with various substances) and their applications in daily life

1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of elements on the basis of their arrangements in the periodic table (a) Explain the changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table
(b) Use the electronic configuration of an element to locate their positions in the periodic table
2.1 Conduct experiments in Chemistry (a) Prepare acid- base indicators using locally available materials
(b) Use the prepared indicators to test acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality

Form Two.main: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
Form Two.competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry (a) Describe the mole concept (comparison of the mole with other units of measurements and molar quantities of substances)

Form Three.competence: (b) Explain Avogadro’s law in relation to molar quantities
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Guide student in manageable groups to use the Avogadros Law in explaining the molar quantities

Form Three.competence: (c) Explain the principles of volumetric analysis (preparation of standard solutions and volumetric calculations)
Form Three.activity: Brainstorming: Assign students to brainstorm on the concept of volumetric analysis Project works: Guide students to carry-out a visit to nearby possible industries eg. Foods, drinks, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals industries to analyse procedures for determining amounts of chemical substances. Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to perform volumetric calculations and make classroom presentations

Form Three.competence: (d) Describe the applications of volumetric analysis in real life and industrial settings as in soft drinks and cocktail making, medicine and in agriculture
Form Three.activity: Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments related to the applications of volumetric analysis

Form Three.competence: (e) Explore the basic tenets of ionic theory and electrolysis (ionic theory, mechanism of electrolysis and laws of electrolysis)
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the concept of ionic theory and electrolysis and make presentations Experimentation: Guide students to carry-out experiments that demonstrate the mechanism of electrolysis using simple available chemicals and apparatus Field Trip: Guide students to carry-out fields trips to near by industries involved in extraction, electroplating and purification of metals and examine the applications of electrolysis

Form Three.competence: (f) Describe the preparation and properties of various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides and sulphates of metals)
Form Three.activity: Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to investigate properties of compound of metals and relate with extraction of metals, making of paints, textiles, drinking water, soaps, and detergents

Form Three.competence: (g) Describe the oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metal compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia, and carbon dioxide)
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the properties of non-metals and write report Project works: Guide students to carry-out visits to nearby industries for making gases, pesticides, fertilisers and other chemicals, analyse properties of the compounds of non-metals

Form Three.competence: 2.1 Conduct experiments in Chemistry (a) Perform experiments on volumetric analysis
Form Three.activity: Experimentation: Guide students to perform titrations for various standard solutions Field trips: Guide students to execute a field trips to nearby industries mainly concerned with quantification of species in different substances and write a report for assessment

Form Three.competence: (b) Perform experiments on the applications of electrolysis in corrosion inhibition and purification of metals
Form Three.activity: Experimentation: Guide students to investigate the applications of electrolysis in the electroplating process for common items in the environment

Form Three.competence: (c) Use appropriate software to sketch the set-ups of experiments
Form Three.activity: Experimentation: Guide students to use various software in sketching experimental set-ups

Form Three.competence: (d) Prepare various compounds of metals (oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, chlorides, and sulphates)
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Organise students in manageable groups to examine different compounds of metals Experimentation: Assign students to prepare various compounds of metals using available chemicals in the laboratory

Form Three.competence: (e) Demonstrate oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metallic compounds (oxygen, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen, ammonia and carbon dioxide)
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Organise students in manageable groups to describe properties of non-metal compounds and make presentations Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to investigate industrial mechanisms involving oxidizing and displacement properties of non-metals

Form Three.competence: (f) Prepare sulphuric acid from sulphur dioxide
Form Three.activity: Experimentation: Guide students to prepare sulphuric acid by using sulphur dioxide

Form Three.main: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic principles of extraction of metals
Form Three.competence: 3.1 Demonstrate mastery of the principles of extraction of metals (a) Describe the extraction of iron from its ore (ores, stages, and methods of extraction)
Form Three.activity: Field trips: Organise students field trips to nearby mining sites/ factories to analyse the process for extraction of iron from its ores and write the report Group discussion: Organise students in manageable groups to describe stages and methods involved in extraction of metals and make presentation

Form Three.competence: 4.1 Conduct a project in Chemistry (a) Design and carry-out a simple research project in Chemistry
Form Three.activity: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to analyse social and scientific challenges such as water pollutions, water purifications, rusting, fire outbreak, pesticides, acid and chemical waste management Project works: Guide students to apply Chemistry principles to investigate on domestic strategies for water purifications, metals purification, metal extraction. and develop local and scientific mechanisms for addressing the identified scientific challenges

Form Four.activity: (a) Explore the basic tenets of qualitative analysis (preliminary analysis, tests in solution and confirmatory test)

Form Four.main: Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry

Form Four.activity: (b) Explore the basic tenets of Organic Chemistry (organic compounds; aliphatic hydrocarbons and alcohols)

Form Four.activity: (a) Use Chemistry software to draw organic structures of hydrocarbons and alcohols with 1 carbon to 10 carbon atoms

Form Four.competence: Use the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry nomenclature to name chemical species
Form Four.activity: (b) Name aliphatic hydrocarbons and alcohols with 1 carbon to 10 carbon atoms using the IUPAC system and Chemistry software

Form Four.competence: Use chemical symbols, formulae and equations to represent chemical reaction
